title: Bind provider-native sessions, compaction, permissions, credentials, billing, and recovery to UNIIMENTE's single canonical control plane
problem: OpenAI and Anthropic added provider-hosted agent state, compaction, and automated permission decisions while Kimi changed billing allocation and reported repeated search degradation; these capabilities can improve workflows but can also create parallel runtime, authority, replay, privacy, and cost paths.
baseline: Kernel main at d7c235ae owns canonical authority, history, task/receipt semantics, and consequence controls; DALEOBANKS main at e2f1ebed has the only active provider adapter found, using OpenAI Chat Completions and optional embeddings; WMI and PumpStation defer constitutional authority to the Kernel.

alternatives.name: Narrow provider capability bindings plus review evidence
alternatives.description: Treat hosted sessions, compaction blocks, permission evaluations, key-expiry metadata, billing allocation, and status events as evidence behind canonical adapters; add no runtime.
advantages: Keeps one source of truth and one authority path
Makes replay, cost, and residency risks reviewable
disadvantages: Requires future adapter fixtures before adoption
alternatives.revival_evidence: Retain unless a simpler existing Kernel contract already proves all mappings without new protocol text.

alternatives.name: Brief only
alternatives.description: Report the material changes without durable repository evidence or protocol rules.
disadvantages: Later agents may reinterpret provider state as authority
No durable compaction or billing-allocation rule
alternatives.revival_evidence: Revive if the protocol is merged elsewhere or a canonical contract already encodes these rules.

alternatives.name: Provider-native agent runtimes
alternatives.description: Use OpenAI Agents API and Claude Managed Agents as independent durable orchestration systems with provider-native permissions and recovery.
advantages: Fast access to hosted orchestration, sandboxes, recovery, and tooling
disadvantages: Duplicates scheduler, history, memory, approvals, and receipts
Creates vendor lock-in and residency constraints
Can execute effects before UNIIMENTE review
alternatives.revival_evidence: Only a founder-approved architecture proving one canonical authority/event/receipt plane and measured superiority over the Kernel baseline could revive it.

alternatives.name: Fixture-only experiment
alternatives.description: Without provider calls, model signed-block, permission, timeout, and billing events as deterministic fixtures mapped into existing canonical records.
advantages: Can falsify mapping assumptions without credentials or external effects
disadvantages: Does not prove live provider behavior
alternatives.revival_evidence: Run only when an owning adapter is proposed and a founder authorizes the bounded experiment.

do_nothing_option.expected_outcome: Current main remains unchanged and the existing draft provider protocol stays stale/conflicted while provider-native state can be adopted later without explicit canonical bindings.
disadvantages: Hosted state or auto permissions may be mistaken for authority
Billing and outage retries may be misclassified

roles.position: Retain the provider capability horizon while binding every new surface to founder-authorized Kernel authority and INTENT-0029's reversible review boundary.
material_concerns: Provider convenience must not narrow or replace the canonical UNIIMENTE destination
No provider change grants production authority
evidence_refs: OpenAI and Anthropic official release notes

roles.position: Use one adapter seam and canonical workflow, event, approval, idempotency, receipt, and cost identities; provider sessions and summaries remain subordinate artifacts.
material_concerns: Provider event IDs replacing canonical identities

roles.position: The strongest competitor is fast but constitutionally unsafe by default: provider auto-permission can execute irreversible effects and hosted recovery can duplicate work.
material_concerns: Authority laundering through provider allow signals
Governance automation becoming de facto policy authority

roles.position: The only direct exposure is DALEOBANKS' existing OpenAI key and non-effectful generation path; record expiry readiness but perform no rotation or routing work.
Provider-signed summaries and safety evaluations are claims, not independent proof; preserve raw and canonical records, protect data classes, and separate unit price from account balances.

evidence.claim: OpenAI released the Agents API public beta and project-key expiration controls on 2026-09-10.
evidence.finding: Hosted durable sessions/orchestration/recovery and key-lifetime controls are available; Agents API is US-residency-only and not ZDR eligible.

evidence.claim: Anthropic released on-demand signed compaction on 2026-09-14 and Managed Agents auto permission evaluation on 2026-09-10.
evidence.finding: Signed summaries replace history in provider requests; auto may execute a tool before human review and is explicitly not a human checkpoint.

evidence.claim: Kimi changed cash/voucher allocation on 2026-09-14 and had repeated search-error incidents from 2026-09-09 through 2026-09-14.
evidence.finding: Public-account cash timing changes without a unit-price change; repeated short search degradation raises retry and duplicate-cost risk.

evidence.claim: The four default branches have no active OpenAI Agents API, Anthropic, or Kimi adapter surface; DALEOBANKS has the only active provider code found.
evidence.reference: GitHub connector searches and file reads at d7c235ae, e2f1ebed, ec82b802, and db6758df
evidence.finding: No exact native-agent/compaction/permission/Kimi-search tokens were found; DALEOBANKS uses gpt-4o-mini and text-embedding-3-small.

counterevidence.claim: Material provider releases require an immediate integration migration.
counterevidence.finding: No direct use of the new hosted agent, compaction, auto-permission, cyber, live, or Kimi search surfaces was found; a runtime migration is not warranted.

counterevidence.claim: Status recovery proves a timed-out or disconnected task is safe to retry.
counterevidence.finding: Status pages report service recovery, not per-request absence, completion, or external-effect reconciliation.

pass_1.intended_outcome: Preserve access to useful provider capabilities while keeping one canonical UNIIMENTE authority, workflow, event, replay, receipt, evaluation, credential, cost, and runtime path.

advantages.statement: Provider-native continuity and compaction can reduce operational work and context cost.
advantages.amplified_value: Used behind one adapter, provider innovations become replaceable capabilities that strengthen rather than fragment the Kernel.

advantages.statement: Permission and status telemetry can improve observability.
advantages.amplified_value: Preserved beside canonical decisions and receipts, it supports independent auditing and safer recovery.

disadvantages.statement: Hosted durable sessions can become a second runtime and source of truth.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Treat every provider session as a revocable leased capability mapped to the existing canonical workflow, event, approval, and receipt identities.

disadvantages.statement: Signed compaction can erase replay evidence or split histories.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Preserve raw blocks, summarized source ranges, canonical cursors, and original event provenance; never delete canonical history.

disadvantages.statement: Provider auto-permission can execute effects before human review.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Prohibit auto for consequence-bearing tools; provider allow remains telemetry and cannot bypass the Consequence Gate.

disadvantages.statement: Key expiry can create availability pressure and unsafe emergency rotation.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Track non-secret expiry metadata and escalate rotation to the credential owner; preserve canonical task identities across key versions.

disadvantages.statement: Outages, background compaction, and recovery can make completion ambiguous and duplicate cost or effects.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Require canonical receipt reconciliation, idempotency continuity, circuit breaking, and recovery canaries before retry or failover.

disadvantages.statement: Recurring review can create low-signal governance churn.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Keep no-material-change/no-PR and kill after one immaterial recurring PR.

comparisons.baseline: Current main has generic recursive governance but no merged provider-change section; PR 91 holds the prior bounded protocol and is behind main.
comparisons.do_nothing: Avoids mutation but leaves hosted-state, compaction, auto-permission, key-expiry, and billing-allocation semantics implicit.
comparisons.simplest_viable_alternative: A brief-only report is lower effort but lacks a durable rule for future adapters and collaborators.
comparisons.strongest_competing_architecture: Provider-native durable agent runtimes maximize feature access but duplicate canonical state, approvals, recovery, and cost paths.
comparisons.reversible_experiment: A fixture-only adapter mapping can test event/receipt/compaction semantics without credentials, network calls, production routing, or a second runtime.

rejected_alternatives.name: Do nothing
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: The new hosted and permission surfaces expose a concrete constitutional ambiguity not stated on current main.
rejected_alternatives.revival_evidence: Revive if an already-merged canonical contract is shown to cover every provider state and permission mapping.

rejected_alternatives.name: Immediate provider-native adoption
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: No direct exposure or measured benefit justifies a second durable control plane, new retention posture, or credential work.
rejected_alternatives.revival_evidence: Founder authorization plus an independently verified adapter experiment that preserves singular authority/runtime and beats baseline on defined outcomes.

rejected_alternatives.name: Immediate credential rotation
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: The review has no authority or account evidence to rotate keys, and the feature does not state that existing keys changed.
rejected_alternatives.revival_evidence: Authorized credential-owner inventory showing an expiry deadline and an approved zero-downtime rotation plan.

pass_2.attack_summary: The Pass-1 mapping layer could still launder provider state into canon, expand cost-account access, overfit mutable prose, or evolve into a standing compatibility scheduler.

new_weaknesses.statement: A canonical adapter can become an unquestioned choke point that silently reinterprets provider state.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Require raw-provider preservation, explicit loss/addition mapping, deterministic fixtures, and an independent evaluator before promotion.

new_weaknesses.statement: Cost or key-readiness reviews could be used to justify unauthorized account or secret access.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Record only repository-visible configuration and public provider rules; account, contract, and secret inspection require separate authorization.

new_weaknesses.statement: Documentation may change in place and make the evidence packet non-reproducible.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Record observation/effective dates, exact surfaces, repository SHAs, and future captured fixtures; treat links as provider claims rather than live proof.

new_weaknesses.statement: A standing compatibility harness could become a duplicate scheduler/runtime.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Permit fixture-only tests invoked by the existing test system; no daemon, queue, provider session owner, or new durable loop.

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: The protocol explicitly makes provider sessions leased capabilities and prohibits canonical ownership or a second scheduler/runtime.
Raw block, source-range, canonical cursor, and original event lineage are mandatory; canonical history is never deleted.
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: Any compaction fixture or adapter proposal

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: Auto permission is not allowed for consequence-bearing tools and cannot bypass Kernel policy or human review.
Only non-secret readiness metadata is in scope; real rotation requires credential-owner authority and account evidence.
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: Known key expiry or founder-authorized credential inventory

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: Canonical receipts, idempotency continuity, circuit breaking, and recovery canaries gate retry and failover.
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: Any timeout, disconnect, background completion, or status recovery

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: The materiality and no-change/no-PR gates bound review noise.
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: One immaterial PR or repeated low-signal brief

pass_2.final_design: Update the existing draft PR 91 rather than create a duplicate PR: reconcile its protocol file with current main, add explicit provider-session, compaction, permission, credential-expiry, cost-allocation, and recovery bindings, and append this source-backed review plus validated deliberation. Make no runtime, provider, credential, account, or production change.

residual_risks.risk: Live configurations and contracts can differ from repository evidence.
residual_risks.mitigation: State the inspection limit and require separate authorized production/account inventory.
residual_risks.review_trigger: Before any migration or credential/account action

residual_risks.risk: One agent performed all five perspectives.
residual_risks.mitigation: Keep the PR draft and require human or independent review before merge or adoption.
Use dated links, exact surfaces, repository SHAs, and captured fixtures in any implementation PR.
residual_risks.review_trigger: Next weekly run or provider adapter proposal

dissent.handling: Preserve the objection in the review and PR; draft-only execution proceeds because it is reversible, but merge and any consequential adoption remain human decisions.

entries.position: Do not let recurring model-authored protocol edits normalize de facto policy authority.
entries.rationale: Even correct draft text can consume founder attention and shift institutional norms without measured benefit.
entries.evidence_threshold: Show that the packet prevents a missed deadline or unsafe retry without producing an immaterial recurring PR; otherwise regress to brief-only review.
entries.review_trigger: Review of PR 91 and immediately after any low-signal PR or boundary violation

migration_plan: No runtime migration. If a provider feature is later proposed, first add a narrow canonical adapter contract and deterministic fixtures, then run a separately authorized sandbox canary with independent evaluation; production routing, credentials, data class, cost ceiling, and rollback require their own founder-approved change.

steps: Leave draft PR 91 unmerged or revert its docs-only commits
Preserve the dated review and dissent as historical evidence
Regress recurring repository edits to brief-only review if the materiality gate fails

kill_criteria: Any write to a default branch or merge without founder approval
Any production, credential, billing-account, contract, or routing change
Any provider-owned canonical workflow, event, approval, memory, receipt, evaluator, or cost ledger
Any second scheduler or durable runtime
Any lost replay lineage, missing receipt, or duplicate external effect
Any consequence-bearing tool allowed solely by provider auto permission
Any ineligible data residency or retention path
Any same-provider sole evaluation of promotion
review_trigger: Founder review of draft PR 91; next material provider change; any proposed provider adapter; any known key expiry; any ambiguous provider completion; or one immaterial recurring PR
